Definition: of uncertain derivation; the north (properly, wind):--north.
BiblicalUsage: The north is the word for the north wind, the quarter of the cold — and it appears twice, both times in the gathering of God's people. In Luke 13:29 they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and sit down in the kingdom of God. In Revelation 21:13 the holy city has gates on the north, three gates, and on the south three gates. The Greek text spells it βορρᾶς, without the rough breathing of the dictionary form, but it is the same word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the north gate is the promise: they come from every quarter, north included, and sit down in the kingdom.
